title: Stage 2 actor service observation architecture
purpose: Add bounded connection-local actor service evidence and a versioned post-service Stage 1 and Stage 2 join without installing a work-quantum policy or changing shard scheduling.
design_summary: A connection can independently opt into actor-service and buffer-copy ObserveOnly sinks. The existing shard records a compact immutable actor value after each complete transition and effect dispatch. A versioned useful-work vector preserves dispatch kind, effects, follow-ons, duration, and queue delay as unlike components without inventing a scalar. A separate connection-local repost gate packs a monotonic generation and closed state into one atomic value; idle requests create one enqueue owner, requests during service coalesce, completion creates at most one new token, stale tokens cannot act, and failed posts or shutdown stop the gate. The gate does not enqueue, preempt, execute, or own protocol work and remains disconnected from the legacy shard until exact remaining-work and cooperative-boundary proofs exist. Existing ownership boundaries record legacy_current retry copies, oversized raw queue copies, formatted payloads, combined payloads, sent-plaintext retention, owned path-migration retransmission clones, receive-segment insertion or capacity reuse, and pooled protected-packet construction with logical and copied bytes, segment and capacity counts, join scope, versions, reason, latch, lifecycle, and explicit missing state. A configure-once connection-local operation observer links retransmission, stream, protection, and hosted endpoint bookkeeping to the runtime evidence sink; both producer and sink failures are guarded so they cannot affect progress or ownership. Fixed-field v3 accumulators build bounded summaries while retained v1 and v2 schemas remain immutable. Compact non-identity lifetime tokens move with each observed owner through authoritative success, failure, cancellation, reset, loss, retransmission, endpoint handoff, terminal cleanup, and disposal. Shared hosted segmentation creates one construction and release for its one shared array rather than one record per slice. The raw host retains separate construction and release records under an exact connection-key and operation-sequence join and emits bounded writer failures explicitly. An eligible epoch callback now occurs only after effect dispatch, follow-on measurement, actor publication, and work-item or connection-event resource release. A versioned boundary repeats the connection epoch sequence and end tick and records source, disposition, actor publication, release completion, and explicit missing or fault state. One guarded accumulator seals the four Stage 1 axis records, actor summary, and buffer summary only when connection observation, receive-credit snapshot, and boundary keys match monotonically. The raw host configures that accumulator for every adaptive execution and emits a joined raw record plus retained compatibility streams. The append-only exporter validates exact joins, unique ordering, four Stage 1 records, and one varied axis; retains checksums and counts; and makes bounded-channel failure an explicit invalid_contract record. The legacy shard drain and copy or ownership paths remain the only applied behavior.
data_and_state_considerations: The observations, useful-work vector, repost token, repost gate, lifetime token, and accumulators use enums, immutable record structs, fixed scalar fields, one packed connection-local atomic state, and connection-local accumulator locks. They introduce no object identity, per-packet dependency injection, dictionary, model, global lock, or unbounded state. Scheduled timer work retains its due tick in an inactive work-item storage slot, preserving the 144-byte work-item layout. Connection-local inter-service gap uses one atomic previous-service timestamp and is never relabeled as continuous runnable time. The application-send queue, sent-packet store, and retransmission queue maintain total retained count, capacity, and oldest time at existing ownership transitions so their total retention snapshots no longer scan; application-send queue-cause and sent-packet storage or packet-number-span detail remain diagnostic scans. Exact buffer release is implemented for all eight closed managed construction paths, including recovery and hosted endpoint ownership of protected arrays. Missing runnable-connection count, oldest shard item age, reviewed scalar useful-work units, exact remaining actor work, Linux unmanaged staging correlation, independently verified kernel-send outcome, retained age outside completed lifetimes, and pool outstanding state remain explicit. Wake grouping is complete only when the run manifest proves full-shard observation coverage.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Observation may measure existing follow-on counts but cannot limit or defer them.
A throwing or rejecting sink cannot interrupt transition, effect, ownership release, cancellation, disposal, recovery, timer, or terminal work.
Queue delay is not oldest-shard-item age, pending work-item count is not runnable-connection count, and inter-service gap is not continuous runnable time or starvation.
The post-service callback may seal Stage 2 summaries only after actor publication and resource release; invalid joins are rejected before reset.
Buffer terminal-release correlation carries only a compact token with the existing owner; it cannot retain object identity, add an outstanding-operation dictionary, or become release authority.
The actor repost gate is an unconnected ownership primitive; it cannot change scheduling until a reviewed caller supplies exact remaining work and enqueues each returned generation exactly once.
Actor_work_quantum remains legacy_current and non-forceable until cooperative checkpoints and exactly-once repost are separately designed and verified.
Buffer_copy_coalescing remains legacy_current and non-forceable until a distinct conservative implementation and exact terminal-release correlation are separately designed and verified.
Active_internal and production activation remain unauthorized.
alternatives_considered: Use existing aggregate metrics as the dataset contract. Rejected because they are not connection-attributable, versioned, or deterministically joinable.
Treat each dequeued event as one equal work unit. Rejected because packet, API, timer, effect, and follow-on costs differ materially.
Add a quantum while instrumenting the loop. Rejected because no exactly-once repost or reviewed preemption seam exists.
Insert the actor summary into the former Stage 1 pre-service epoch callback. Rejected because that callback occurred before complete actor service and would shift or truncate attribution.
risks: Observation overhead can perturb hot shard paths; disabled-path and later manual or nightly allocation checks remain required.
Partial per-connection coverage can be mistaken for complete wake membership; manifests must declare coverage.
A post-service fault can leave incomplete outcome information; bounded fault disposition remains explicit.
Primitive counts can be mistaken for a reviewed scalar quantum; UsefulWorkUnitsUndefined prevents that claim.
open_questions: Which bounded shard-pressure snapshot can expose runnable connection count and oldest item age without a global lock?
Which transition, effect, and follow-on boundaries can supply exact remaining work and yield while preserving timer, recovery, terminal, cancellation, disposal, and buffer-ownership priority?
